chunks: Muhammad ibn Ahmad ibn Yahya narrated from Ahmad, al-'Abbas, and al-Haytham together, from al-Hasan ibn Mahbub, from 'Ali ibn al-Fudayl, from Abu 'Abd Allah عليه السلام, who said:

If a man is found killed among the tribe of a people, they shall all swear that they did not kill him and that they do not know any killer for him. If they refuse to swear, they are held liable for the blood-money, divided among them from their wealth equally, among all the adult men of the tribe.

key_terms.الدِّيَةَ: the prescribed blood-money due in compensation for unlawful killing
key_terms.الْقَبِيلَةِ: the tribe or collective group among whom the slain person was found
key_terms.الْمُدْرِكِينَ: those who are legally adult and accountable
key_terms.حَلَفُوا: they swore an oath in a legal setting
key_terms.قَاتِلًا: the one responsible for the killing
key_terms.مَقْتُولٌ: a person who has been killed

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling if a murdered man is found among a tribe and the killer is unknown?
ai.summary: This hadith states a judicial ruling for a case in which a slain person is found among a tribe and the killer is unknown. The tribe must swear that they neither killed him nor know his killer; if they refuse, the diyah is imposed collectively upon the adult men of the tribe from their property.
